plan.summary: Replace the bool(value) implementation in parse_enabled with a module-level immutable data mapping that recognizes only the tokens 'true' and 'false', so accepted boolean values are data-driven rather than branch-based and no new token is accepted.
steps: Define a module-level dict mapping the accepted tokens 'true' and 'false' to their boolean values in src/parser.py.
Rewrite parse_enabled to return the mapping entry for the given value via direct indexing, which rejects any token outside {'true', 'false'}.
Confirm the registered parser-contract check passes: parse_enabled('true') is True and parse_enabled('false') is False.
risks: Direct dict indexing raises KeyError for empty or unrecognized input instead of returning a bool; this is intentional to refuse new tokens, but it changes the prior permissive behavior for invalid input.
The mapping is keyed on exact case-sensitive strings, so any expectation of case-insensitive matching would break; this is required to avoid accepting new tokens.

answer.summary: Refactored parse_enabled to accept only the boolean tokens 'true' and 'false' via an immutable module-level dict lookup, removing the bool(value) branching. This makes accepted tokens data-driven and ensures no new token is accepted, so parse_enabled('true') is True and parse_enabled('false') is False.
